title: Spark Asset Foundation legally owns the liquidity layer's funds and may delegate credit underwriting to Phoenix Labs
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.8.2.6 states the ownership plainly: "**Spark Asset Foundation is the legal owner of funds allocated via the Spark Liquidity Layer** and onboarded entity for custodians and collateral agents," empowered to exercise all rights "for the benefit of the Spark ecosystem and according to generally accepted business practices and Spark Asset Foundation's professional judgement." A.6.1.1.1.3.7.2.6 says the same for the Arkis relationship.

Then the delegation: the Foundation "may delegate certain operational functions to **Phoenix Labs** at its discretion, including **risk underwriting, sourcing prospective borrowers, and deal negotiation**."

Two layers separate SPK holders from the capital. Legal title sits with a foundation, because a custodian cannot onboard a token-holder collective and a court cannot enforce a loan agreement signed by one — off-chain lending is impossible without a legal person. And the substantive credit decisions — who borrows, on what terms, at what risk — may be performed by a contributor firm operating under the Foundation's discretion rather than under a governance mandate.

What governance retains is the *envelope*: approved assets, LTV ladders, exposure limits, rate floors, venues, and the mandatory-recall rules, all amendable only by Root Edit. Within that envelope, individual deals are not voted on. The Artifact does not require Phoenix Labs' underwriting to be published, reviewed by the Spark Risk Council, or reported per loan.

The standard applied is "generally accepted business practices" and "professional judgement" — a fiduciary formulation, not a rule. That is the honest way to describe a discretionary mandate, but it means the binding constraints on Spark's off-chain lending are the numeric parameters in this Artifact plus the good faith of two entities SPK holders do not directly control.
description: The Foundation is the onboarded entity for custodians and exercises all rights on professional judgement, and may hand risk underwriting, borrower sourcing and deal negotiation to a contributor firm.
